The imaginary-superposition Fourier control on representative zero instead gives measured-versus-compiled total variation from 0.996336 to 0.997313 across its three repeats, while its measured-versus-preceding-compiled distance is 0.030785 to 0.034049.

The historical JSON's one-click label denotes that occupation-sum selection; the mixed threshold/quasi-PNR documentation does not establish a uniform physical-click model. The records establish a compilation-metadata/measurement mismatch, rather than which applied-control or result-association mechanism caused it. Fixed request ordering confounds a setting-specific response with a preceding-setting effect. The analysis supplies neither calibrated uncertainty coverage, absolute transmission, process tomography nor fundamental quaternionic-physics evidence. claims.statement: On the executed Fez and Kingston ripple atlas circuits at IBM's executed pulse times, six coherent error families (frame detuning, CZ conditional phase, static ZZ in the partner-in-0 and symmetric frames, SX amplitude and axis tilt) fitted one at a time to the edge fringe phase offsets of all 14 lanes leave every lane except two (Fez lane 5 with axis tilt, Kingston lane 2 with detuning and with partner-in-0 ZZ) above 1.5 times its leave-one-out noise floor under every single family, the lowest ratio per lane ranging from 1.68 to 3.70, so no single family accounts for the offsets; partner-in-0 ZZ scores below the symmetric frame on 13 of 14 lanes in the linear fit and on all 14 resimulated, by a median factor of 2.4, and is the best single family on 7 lanes (detuning on 4, axis tilt on 3), while SX amplitude beats the lane mean on none.

claims.boundary: One 16384-shot run per circuit, the three batches minutes apart on the calibration after the platform's benchmarking, so drift between batches enters the case contrasts; the exclusion forced longer routes (75 to 91 CZ against 66 to 70 in the three-region placement), so the comparison with the earlier placement changes depth and qubits together and does not separate them; the per-region split rests on one replica per case and region; dark + bright - 1 = -0.009 (z = -2.3) and fixture - 1/2 = -0.008 (z = -3.0) repeat the earlier series' shift toward selector 1; the readout correction uses all-|0> and all-|1> circuits, which omit readout crosstalk under the witness's state.

claims.statement: On the noiseless QX emulator the readout ring-down dry run reports 'not detected' on both series under the preregistered rule: all 10 targets are usable at visibility 1, every |delta(tau)| is at most 13.6 kHz against 4.7 kHz standard errors, chi2(H1) runs 0.25 to 10.96 on 5 degrees of freedom (60.3 on 50 summed over targets), and the largest chi2(H1) - chi2(H2) is 6.02, below the 13.82 threshold. QX returned its 10-character measurement register for circuits declaring bit[20], so the mid-circuit outcomes were absent and the postselected cross-check did not run.
claims.boundary: An ideal state-vector emulator at 2048 shots per circuit, one run per circuit in 18 batches; it tests parsing, submission, collection, the analysis and the decision rule on data whose answer is zero, and establishes nothing about Tuna-17's readout, its register width or the postselected cross-check. The decision rule was fixed in the cases before submission; the all-shot estimator replaced the postselected one after these data showed the measurement register, which changes no circuit byte and leaves the rule's text unchanged, and on these data the two coincide because no mid-circuit bit returned.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 series P (targets Q0, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q16, 8192 shots per circuit) the preregistered rule reports 'not detected': 7 targets are usable (Q5 fails the 0.3 visibility floor), 3 classify as tails (Q6, Q10, Q16) and 2 as static offsets (Q11, Q12), below the 50% threshold. No classified target fits H2 (chi2 30.7 to 193.7 on 3 degrees of freedom); Q11's readout arms sit 19 to 33 kHz below its reference at every tau out to 2 us.

The rule compares H2 with H1 and tests neither model's fit, so the tail and offset classes mark arm-to-arm structure beyond shot noise rather than a residual-photon decay. claims.statement: Tuna-17 returns the full bit register: bit[34] circuits on qubit[17] came back as 34-character strings carrying every mid-circuit outcome. On 2026-10-17, Q9's idle P1 rose from 0.02-0.05 to 0.27-0.29 from 04:06Z and stayed there through 05:33Z, and after the 04:12Z platform calibration Q0 and Q6 prepared in |1> read 0.39 and 0.14 after a 2 us wait (0.85 and 0.67 at 03:39Z) while their idle P1 stayed below 0.04.

claims.statement: Q9's elevated idle P1 on Tuna-17 from 04:06Z on 2026-10-17 is misassignment of |0> that leaves the qubit in |0>. Same-batch idle and X readouts bound, at one-sided 3-sigma binomial limits, e0 >= 0.19 in the three zero-wait batches (0.145 with a 2 us wait) against e0 <= 0.030 before the change, and the excited population p <= 0.115. In series Q at zero delay, shots whose opening readout of Q9 gave 1 end an X90 pair at the level of opening-0 shots: excited fraction w = 0.021 +- 0.013 over 2122 opening-1 shots, where the other eight targets read -0.10 to 0.20.
claims.boundary: The bounds assume p <= 1/2, an X that inverts at most fully and idle and X readouts from one batch; the herald test reads the zero-delay arm, because relaxation during a longer delay pulls w toward 0, and its opening readout is a mid-circuit readout taken with nine targets read at once, at 04:39Z.

claims.statement: After the 04:12Z platform calibration of 2026-10-17, the zero-wait P(1|1) of Q0 and Q6 at 05:26-05:33Z keeps 0.55 and 0.16 of the excited scale read before the change, and that loss is not relaxation inside the 800 ns readout: relaxation would need T1 <= 1.36 and 0.44 us and leave P(1|1) <= 0.156 and 0.015 after a 2 us wait, where the 2 us wait runs read 0.389-0.393 and 0.140-0.144 (z >= 32).
claims.boundary: Assumes the device is unchanged between the 2 us wait runs (04:15-04:24Z) and the zero-wait runs (05:26-05:33Z), and that a qubit surviving the whole readout window reads 1 at the pre-change scale, which bounds T1 for any discriminator response.

claims.statement: P1 after X X with no wait, beside a readout-0 and readout-1 pair in one Tuna-17 batch, separates an under-rotated X from |1> misassignment on Q0 and Q6: under-rotation by the angle their zero-wait P(1|1) implies predicts 0.98 and 0.52, misassignment 0.038 and 0.013. Ramsey inverted with the matched calibration cannot separate them when X and X90 share the under-rotation, because the raw quadratures then take the readout-scale form sin^2(beta) (1 + cos phi) / 2; a fault confined to native X keeps the X90 Ramsey at the earlier scale, which Q6's raw quadrature mean (0.064 against a floor of 0.148) excludes and Q0's (0.287 against 0.175) does not.
claims.boundary: The predictions use the 05:26-05:33Z state; Tuna recalibrates between user jobs, so a run first checks that its readout pair still shows the fault, and leakage, whose X train plateaus instead of oscillating, needs X trains of three and more.

claims.statement: The Ry emulator rejects any bit declaration, assigned or not ('error interpreting cQASM script'), and fails a measure statement at compilation ('not in the primitive gate set'); X, H, CNOT, Rz and an asm(Rydberg) INIT block run, with outcome distributions within total-variation distance 0.035 of the ideal at 1024 shots.

claims.statement: In the pre-T0 batch on Tuna-17 (4096 shots per circuit, jobs finished 15:38Z) the Q0 and Q6 readout fault of the morning is absent: Q0 reads P(1|1) 0.973 and Q6 0.957 against the precondition limits 0.7 and 0.3, and Q9 reads P(1|0) 0.018, so the precondition reports fault-recovered and the double-X discriminator is not read. Every qubit of the admitted layout {1, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14} passes the T0 readout rule (readout-1 P1 0.912 to 0.975, readout-0 P1 at most 0.045), and q5, q6, q7 and q9 are readout-admissible; q5, q6 and q7 keep their Ramsey visibility exclusion.
claims.boundary: One batch on one calibration, taken after the platform benchmarking the operator observed at 15:34Z; the readout state can change at the next calibration. The double-X P1 values it records (Q0 0.019, Q6 0.110) are not a discriminator reading, since the precondition failed, and the proposed discriminator claim proposed-tuna17-q0-q6-double-x-discriminator stays untested. Readout admission lifts no visibility exclusion.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 the reduced two-label LCU of edge (1,10)(4,15) of kite 3, corrected per batch with its own readout pair, keeps a contrast C(1) = 0.954 +- 0.003, C(5) = 0.857 +- 0.003 and C(9) = 0.710 +- 0.003 over a 3 x 3 Latin square of pairs {(1,4), (10,13), (12,14)} and batches at 16384 shots, so the per-CZ retention is r = 0.9654 with 99% bootstrap interval [0.9638, 0.9671], inside the decision band [0.87, 0.97] as preregistered and above its prediction [0.87, 0.96]. The depth-1 upper bound 0.961 clears the 0.5 floor, so the program continues; C(1) and r both miss their predictions ([0.72, 0.82] and [0.87, 0.96]) upward. The QX twins of the three witness circuits read every replica's predicted outcome in all 2048 shots.
claims.boundary: One calibration, three pairs and one edge; the dark replica of each depth sits on one pair and batch, so C(n) carries that pair's offset, and a pair x depth interaction stays inside r. The upward miss of C(1) comes from the prediction, which carried the selector's raw readout factor (about 0.87) while C(n) is readout-corrected; 0.82 / 0.874 = 0.94. Every bright replica cleared the depth-1 bright floor.

claims.statement: Programs of H, CNOT, Z, S, X and Rz on up to 9 atoms run on the Ry emulator when they carry no bit register and no measure statement, the cause of the earlier 'error interpreting cQASM script' failures. Shallow reduced-LCU replicas (one CNOT) read their ideal outcome at a fraction of 0.978 or more and the P = 1/2 replicas sit inside |z| < 4.5; the 9-atom teleport program R9 completes with 77 of 1024 shots (7.5%) outside its ideal support; the full Design B witness of (1,10)(4,15) reads P(selector = 0) 0.270 dark and 0.656 bright, a contrast of 0.387, below the 0.9 ideal-fraction floor, so the smoke series stops there as an emulator rate.
claims.boundary: One run per circuit on the emulator as served on 2026-10-17 at 1024 shots; the Ry error model is undocumented, so the loss with depth is reported as an emulator rate and never as an algebraic result.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 the packed follow series (7 batches, 21 jobs at 16384 shots, readout brackets in batches 0, 3 and 6 that moved at most 0.0076) gives every preregistered decision the census predicts. The reduced two-label LCU classifies all six rows: the kite-3 edge D = -0.964, -0.953, -0.916 on (1,4), (10,13), (12,14), its kite-6 twist D = +0.967, +0.952, the strut D = 0.001 (SE 0.002 to 0.004). Twist equality holds in all four block x setting crossovers at shot noise without a pair allowance: |Delta| at most 0.0040, |z| at most 2.44 against 3. Every depth-1 X conditional coherence has the census sign (E_0 = -1 bright, E_1 = +1 dark), and all eight strut branch expectations lie inside 0.1 + 3 sigma. Both associator walks read <X_c> with the sign of omega = -1 (-0.784 +- 0.006 on star 14 {11, 12, 16}, 6 CZ; -0.937 +- 0.006 on path 4 {1, 2}, 4 CZ), their omit-last controls stay inside 0.1 + 3 sigma, and the walk magnitudes 0.819 and 0.938 lie inside 0.10 of T0's r^n_CZ (0.810, 0.869). The five QX twin batches read every deterministic replica's outcome in all 2048 shots.
claims.boundary: One calibration of one evening (23:08Z to 23:29Z), three pairs, one edge, its twist and one strut, and two walk exemplars. The twist test differences replicas of one batch, so drift between batches cancels; the classification and coherence signs are deterministic-limit decisions that the batch-to-batch scatter of the exploratory claim does not reach. The cross-predicted magnitudes are reported, not decided: two depth-1 X coherences on (10,13) read |E| = 1.10 after readout correction, outside the 0.954 +- 0.10 band, because the bracket's e10 for q13 exceeds its witness-context value (claim qi-tuna17-boxkite-follow-ladder-drift).

claims.statement: The follow series' reported estimates and their limits on Tuna-17. Coherence ladder (CZ depths 1, 5, 9; unweighted fits, 99% shot-noise intervals): r_coh = 0.962 and 0.957, r_pop = 0.925 and 0.915, r_coh / r_pop = 1.040 and 1.047 on (1,4) and (10,13); on (12,14) r_coh = 0.908 while 2 Pc(9) - 1 is negative, so r_pop is undefined; the phase slope per CZ lies within [-0.008, 0.008] rad on every pair. The X and Y replicas of one depth-9 bright edge, which run in consecutive batches and share the selector marginal, differ by 0.024 to 0.033 on all three pairs (4 to 7 shot-noise sigma), against at most 0.014 at depth 5 and 0.007 at depth 1, so deep-circuit populations scatter between batches by about 0.03 beyond shot noise and the ladder intervals understate the uncertainty; r_coh / r_pop above 1 and Pc(12,14, depth 9) = 0.483 below 1/2 are not established. Against T0 seven and a half hours earlier (no retained record places a platform calibration between them), the bright-edge populations moved by -0.209 on (12,14) at depth 9, -0.106 on (10,13) at depth 5 and -0.042 on (1,4) at depth 9, beyond that scatter. The q13 readout-1 bracket gives e10 = 0.091 while the bright (10,13) coherence's raw -0.911 corrects to -1.105, so the all-qubit readout pair misstates q13's |1> misassignment in the witness context. The walk controls carry phases of 0.297 +- 0.010 rad (star) and 0.052 +- 0.009 rad (path) about omega. The 21 jobs executed in 243.3 s against the design's 233.6 s.
claims.boundary: Descriptive summaries of the retained follow runs; nothing here was a preregistered decision. The bootstrap carries shot and readout-bracket noise only. The q13 discrepancy has two candidate mechanisms that this design does not separate: readout that depends on the state of neighboring qubits (readout-1 excites all 17) and a preparation error of readout-1's own X on q13. The walk phases identify no CZ window or detuning, since each CZ adds its residual local phase. The path omit control reads -0.119 against a limit of 0.126 and one strut branch +0.135 against 0.136: inside the preregistered null offset, though far from 0 on shot noise. The retained shot order carries a 50 Hz modulation that grows with CZ depth (claim qi-tuna17-shot-record-50hz-line), so the ladder's decay mixes decoherence with a time-averaged oscillating phase. A within-batch ladder demodulated at the line is the prospective test of r_coh / r_pop.

claims.statement: The retained per-shot outcome lists of Tuna-17 jobs carry a line at the 50 Hz grid frequency in wall-clock time. A band scan at 0.019 to 0.021 cycles per shot finds the line (whitened, p below 1e-6 after the band's look-elsewhere factor) in 72 of 159 Tuna-17 jobs and in none of 113 QX jobs, none of 51 readout circuits (readout-0, readout-1 and the context readouts, at up to 131072 shots) and none of the 8 depth-1 LCU circuits; it appears in Ramsey, CZ-ladder, walk, additivity and Walsh-exemplar circuits, with first-harmonic amplitudes in P(1) up to 0.43 (q7, ring-down Ramsey) and 0.39 (q5, coupler-ZZ Ramsey). Across the readout ring-down arms, whose circuits differ only in a wait of tau cycles of 20 ns, the peak frequency rises with tau at 50.4 +- 4.0 Hz (31 jobs, one intercept per batch): 12.6 standard errors from the 0 Hz a shot-index-locked source predicts and 0.1 from 50 Hz, which at 50 Hz puts one shot at 402.9 to 404.6 us in the ring-down circuits and 400.7 us in the follow series. In the follow series the bright-edge selectors on (1,4), (10,13) and (12,14) oscillate with amplitudes 0.19 to 0.26 at CZ depth 9, 0.09 to 0.13 at depth 5 and below 0.0175 at depth 1, in phase across the three pairs (resultant 0.996 to 1.000 per job). Within-job stationarity (16 block means per bit, the smallest per-bit chi-square tail times the bits scanned) falls below 0.01 in 11 to 33 percent of the box-kite pre-T0, T0, follow and Walsh-exemplar jobs and in 61 to 75 percent of the morning ring-down jobs. The detection statistic whitens the scanned bits by their same-shot correlation matrix, so correlated bits of one shot do not inflate it.
claims.boundary: A reanalysis of retained shot order, which the platform does not document as temporal; the wall-clock slope is the evidence that it is. The mechanism is inferred, not measured: a 50 Hz modulation common to the chip that grows with the phase a circuit accumulates (wait or CZ count) fits mains-frequency interference on the qubits' frequency or the flux pulses, but no retained probe separates flux pickup from any other 50 Hz path, and the third-harmonic amplitudes do not separate a 150 Hz component from the nonlinear response to a large phase swing. A time-averaged oscillating phase lowers a job's mean contrast, so the follow ladder's decay rates and r_coh / r_pop mix decoherence with this modulation. The scan detects lines in one band only.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 the |1> misassignment of q13 depends on the preparation context of the chip: e10 reads 0.0895 and 0.0863 with all 17 qubits excited (readout-1, batches 0 and 6) against 0.0441 and 0.0399 with q1, q13 and q14 alone excited and every coupled neighbor in |0> (readout-iso-x), differences 0.045 and 0.046 at about 45 standard errors, so context is established on q13 by the preregistered rule (above 0.02 and 5 SE in both brackets). It is absent on q1 (-0.0009, -0.0016) and q14 (-0.0027, -0.0006). The preparation path is absent under the 0.02 threshold on all three: e10 after H Z H minus the interpolated isolated e10 is +0.016 (q13), +0.005 (q14) and -0.0002 (q1). Corrected with the readout-1 brackets, the depth-1 X conditional coherence on (10,13) reads -1.104 and -1.060 (batches 1 and 4); corrected with q13's isolated e10 it reads -0.997 and -0.955, within one of the physical bound; (12,14) reads -0.995 and -0.994 with readout-1 and -0.999 and -0.995 with q14's isolated e10. The follow series' unphysical -1.105 on (10,13) is therefore a calibration artifact of the all-qubit readout-1 bracket applied to q13.
claims.boundary: One device state of one night (01:55Z to 03:02Z, 2026-10-18) at 131072 shots per job. readout-1 and readout-iso-x differ both in the neighbors' state at measurement and in the X pulses applied to the neighbors, so the design does not separate state-dependent readout of q13 from drive crosstalk of those pulses on q13's preparation; readout-1 also excites q10 and q11 together, so it does not say which neighbor matters. The preparation differences below the 0.02 threshold are significant on shot noise (q13 +0.016 at about 20 SE, q14 +0.005 at about 9 SE) and are reported, not decided. Beside an excited q13, q10's own e01 rises by 0.011 to 0.014 against readout-0 (reported).

claims.statement: The within-batch Latin-square ladder on Tuna-17 (every circuit holding CZ depths 1, 5 and 9 on the pairs (1,4), (10,13) and (12,14); X batches 1 and 4, Y batches 2 and 5; 131072 shots per job) gives rho = r_coh / r_pop above 1 on all three pairs in both X batches: 1.021 and 1.020 on (1,4), 1.021 and 1.022 on (10,13), 1.005 and 1.006 on (12,14), each 99% interval excluding 1 (preregistered decision: above 1). The replicate difference exceeds 3 combined standard errors on (12,14) only (z -3.85; (1,4) 1.59, (10,13) -2.68). r_pop is 0.951 to 0.957 on (1,4), 0.953 to 0.958 on (10,13) and 0.976 to 0.978 on (12,14) across all four Latin batches. The 50 Hz line is detected in all 12 Latin jobs, as predicted; the depth-9 over depth-1 amplitude margin holds in 10 of 12 jobs and is refuted in the two jobs whose depth-9 pair is (12,14) in batches 4 and 5 (batch-04 latin-x-1 and batch-05 latin-y-1), where that selector's first harmonic falls to 0.0027.
claims.boundary: rho above 1 means the population contrast decays faster than the joint coherence, which neither a global depolarizing channel (rho = 1) nor dephasing (rho below 1) gives; a coherent error that moves selector population, or the 50 Hz modulation averaged over a job, would raise it, and the design isolates neither. The preregistered rho uses the readout-1 correction, which overstates q13's e10 (claim qi-tuna17-boxkite-ladder-readout-context); with every iso qubit's e10 from readout-iso-x, rho reads 1.021 and 1.020 on (1,4), 1.020 and 1.022 on (10,13), 1.005 and 1.006 on (12,14), each 99% interval again excluding 1, so the decision is the same under both corrections. The line refutation is of the preregistered first-harmonic margin; the second harmonic of the same selector stays at 0.020 to 0.022 (claim qi-tuna17-boxkite-ladder-drift-harmonics), so the refutation does not show the modulation absent.

claims.statement: Descriptive readings of the ladder series. Against the follow series about two and a half hours earlier, the bright-edge populations rose by 0.071 (1,4), 0.092 (10,13) and 0.394 (12,14) at CZ depth 9 and by 0.003, 0.035 and 0.190 at depth 5; (12,14) at depth 9 moved from 0.483 to 0.877. The (12,14) selector at depth 9 carries a first harmonic of 0.024 and 0.026 in batches 1 and 2 and 0.0027 in batches 4 and 5, while its second harmonic stays at 0.020 to 0.022 in all four (shot-record lock-in at each job's peak). In the shot-record scan the 21 ladder jobs fall below an adjusted block-stationarity p of 0.01 in 52 percent of jobs, and none of the 9 readout circuits carries the line at 131072 shots.
claims.boundary: Descriptive; nothing here was a preregistered decision. A first harmonic that vanishes while the second persists fits a static phase moving onto an extremum of the selector's response, inferred, not measured. No retained record places a platform calibration between the follow and ladder series; batch 4 waited about 30 minutes in the queue.

claims.statement: On sim:belenos (its default noise model g2 0.003, indistinguishability 0.92, transmittance 0.06) the six S1 box-kite circuits reproduce their exact Q(sqrt2) ideals: bright a = 1 (5003/4996/0/0), dark a = 0 (Wilson upper bound 0.00038), strut a = 0.506 against 1/2, the one-hot 16D dark pair 0 clicks on all 16 algebra labels, and two-photon label fractions of 0.472 (edge) and 0.0134 (strut), whose strut inversion gives V = 0.918 against the simulator's 0.92.
claims.boundary: One job per circuit on sim:belenos as served on 2026-10-17; the simulator applies its own noise model and Quandela's transpiler, so agreement shows the cases, runner and compilation path are correct, never that hardware reaches the ideal.

claims.statement: On qpu:belenos the bright block that sim:belenos reproduces exactly, sent as a 4-mode unitary inside a 24-mode identity and compiled to the same 552-beam-splitter circuit, keeps 0.470 (Wilson 0.460 to 0.480) of one-click samples on its four modes, and of those an algebra share a = 0.256 (0.244 to 0.269) against the ideal 1; the leaked clicks fall mostly on modes 14 to 19, whose dark counts are below 0.2 per second.
claims.boundary: One 10000-sample job at the 2026-10-17 calibration (HOM 92.6 %, g2 1 %). The root-cause record (docs/evidence/quandela/belenos_leakage_rca.json) refutes a circuit, encoding, convention or multi-photon cause: the decoded compiled mesh reproduces the ideal, and no single-parameter error model reaches the shot-noise floor; the exact replay after a calibration reproduces the leak, and 64 random meshes of the same session show errors about a fifth the size the leak needs, so the leak stays specific to this job's form or mesh.

claims.statement: On sim:belenos an iterated job runs every iteration for one credit and compiles each iteration separately (eight distinct meshes in one fringe job); the edge block's fringe over phi = k pi/4 has visibility 0.996 and offset -0.008 rad and the strut block's is flat (visibility 0.023), and the bright block sent as a compact 4-mode unitary, compact native gates or 24-mode native gates reads a = 1 each while every form compiles to the full 552-splitter mesh.
claims.boundary: Five sim:belenos jobs on 2026-10-17 under the simulator's default noise model; they establish the job, iteration and compilation behavior of the service, never hardware performance.

claims.statement: Quandela Cloud re-transpiles every circuit sent to sim:belenos, the Belenos architecture with its 574 phases bound per iteration (job 1d7160c1, 16 settings) and the same architecture as a numeric circuit (job e5b74123): every returned computed_circuit changes all 574 phases and keeps only the occupied input column (|U|^2 within 2e-4), each setting's histogram lies within shot noise of its ideal (TVD 0.0002 to 0.038 at 1500 samples), and the efficiency-weighted likelihood computed on the returned meshes names the ideal model 352 nats ahead of coupler noise.
claims.boundary: Two sim:belenos jobs on 2026-10-17 with perceval-quandela 1.3.1 against a platform running 1.3.0 and exqalibur 1.4.2; the served meshes match exqalibur's CircuitOptimizer statistically, not bitwise, and the identical sim and QPU meshes hold for the one-circuit single/job-04 body; the iterated job-02 body returned different meshes on qpu:belenos (qd-belenos-same-meshes-drift-between-jobs).

claims.statement: On sim:belenos one 16-iteration job (32b28fe8) carries all 168 zero products and 168 bright controls of the 84 box-kite edges, certified through cd_core and mapped to 8 dark and 8 bright one-photon configurations: every dark configuration reads algebra share a = 0 (0 of 1500 one-click samples, Wilson upper bound 0.0026) and every bright one a = 1 (lower bound 0.9974) through the meshes the service re-transpiled, and the class analysis of the returned meshes reads ideal (p = 0.136).
claims.boundary: One sim:belenos job on 2026-10-18 under the simulator's default noise model; it shows the 84/84 case, the iterated mesh vehicle and the analysis reproduce the exact ideals end to end, never that hardware does.

claims.statement: On qpu:belenos the exact Q1 bright-block body, re-run after the calibration that moved the HOM figure from 92.6 % to 57.6 % with unchanged couplers, compiled to the identical circuit (sha256 9bbbaf63) and kept 0.504 (Wilson 0.494 to 0.514) of one-click samples on the block's four modes against Q1's 0.470 (0.460 to 0.480), with the leaked light again mostly on modes 17, 18 and 19; the HOM figure does not index this one-photon route's leakage.
claims.boundary: Two 10000-sample jobs on one compiled mesh, before and after one calibration; raw in-block shares only, since the receipt's dark rates that the dark-corrected figures subtract are refuted by the C1 runs (modes 0 and 1 read no clicks where they predict about 150 and 40). claims.statement: A proposed confirmatory cross-check of the retained exploratory coupler map uses a gate-level conditional-Ramsey case covering all 24 edges of the retained Tuna-17 coupling graph in eight induced matchings, with both probe directions, static neighbor states 0 and 1, X/Y quadratures, six identical physical delay values including zero, and full four-state joint readout calibration. Hardware batches contain at most three circuits and are acquired sequentially under the current repository policy; a compact QX preflight has its own proposed case and budget. The Q1/Q2 nonedge and driven crosstalk require additional controls. All six delays must pass signal and phase guards; failed precision is inconclusive, not a null. Rates are conditional on the first-interval absolute range below 1 MHz, since the commensurate grid cannot identify all out-of-range aliases. The two probe directions are separate settings, not a simultaneous two-equatorial-qubit Ramsey experiment. Primitive timing sums are planning scenarios, not billed QPU time. Joint readout correction assumes assignment-channel stability across the calibration and Ramsey batches; the estimator does not remove between-batch drift. QX success would support ideal marginal gate and wiring conformance only. The retained exploratory map already found low coherence on some probes at 2 us; requiring signal at all six delays through 40 us can therefore yield inconclusive edges. Its results do not relax the prospective guards. The 139-batch version is not recommended for unchanged acquisition after the retained coherence and calibration changes; no shorter pilot is generated or authorized here. A future revision must set its own prospective thresholds rather than relax this estimator after observing data.

claims.boundary: The preregistered segmented-sweep.json refuses every member (the bound reader kept a barrier before INIT on the ibm_fez table); the verdicts come from the amended analyzer at closure 759d82d74c57 (correcting closure 6d59d710eb61's unconverged fits) and the switching time from a post hoc shot-order analysis, so neither confirms. The near-equal weights fixed over a shot fit charge-parity splitting, which a parity-resolved readout would test; a dispersively coupled two-level fluctuator switching in tens of ms predicts the same telegraph. Shot-to-shot correlation at 9.7 ms makes the per-shot Wald statistics anti-conservative; the non-rejections and the model and alias margins survive that.

claims.statement: The registered finite exact calculations give derivation dimension 14, chosen-octonion stabilizer dimension 8, occupation dimensions 1/3/3/1 and complex Clifford image dimension 64. claims.statement: The frozen BDSC qualification job tc-*-e1 (12 iterations of the 77-parameter ladder-union circuit, 300000 samples each, QRNG seeds) ran end to end on sim:belenos under both policies: the empty-list job 19f18f8c in 148 s and the provider-default rerun cac942bd in 153 s, 1 credit each. One timeout in two provider-default runs establishes no rate; Perceval computes the same noisy distribution in 0.1 s locally, so the stall is placed in the service worker by inference.

The forensic reading (docs/notes/quandela/bdsc-acceptance-diagnostics.md, rated moderate) takes the 0.035 spread of the superpositions about their common drop as a per-compilation response and leaves the common drop of 0.024 unsplit between the device, its characterization and the default policy's processing. The backend reported calibrating at 11:32 UTC, between batches 06 and 08, which fits a recalibration as the cause of the drift but is not established by any retained probe. claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (station control 50.0.0, calibration set 9069c4ef), two jobs of X and a bare measure on QB1 at 2000 shots each billed ceil(runtime), not ceil(the compiler's execution runtime estimate): 2 s for a 1.306 s runtime under passive reset and 1 s for 0.205 s under active_reset_cycles 1, against estimates of 2.804 s and 1.617 s, 1.50 credits in all. The estimates follow 1.60 s per job plus each shot's schedule within 0.02 s. Execution took 316 us per shot under passive reset and 37.5 us under active reset. Active reset left the bare measure at P(1) 0.0680 against 0.0065 under passive reset (difference 0.0615, z 10.4), so one active-reset cycle does not keep QB1's initialization. The passive job read X at 0.9705 and the bare measure at 0.0065, within three standard errors of the calibration-built predictions 0.9817 and 0.0046 (z -2.96 and +1.06).

The excess bare-measure P(1) under active reset is not separated into residual excitation and reset-induced readout error. The H4 bare-measure prediction in the design document was the simulator's 2000-shot sample 0.003; the decision uses the exact unheralded P(1|0) 0.0046. claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (calibration set 9069c4ef, 199 CZ on QB6, QB7, QB10, QB11, QB12, QB16 and QB17, one active-reset cycle with all-zeros heralding keeping 55.9 % of shots), the structure-matched signed probe of the certified sedenion kernel u = (e4 - e15)/sqrt2 of L(e1+e10) read the odd part (Z(t) - Z(-t))/2 of its control at +0.0220 +- 0.0067 for |t| = 0.25 (z 3.29, the sign of t resolved) and +0.0058 +- 0.0030 for |t| = 0.05 (z 1.94, unresolved), so the dilation overlap Re<v|B(t)|u> = t/(2 + |t|) is not falsified and the device carries its sign at |t| = 0.25. Both odd parts fit one visibility, V = 0.206 +- 0.054 times t/(2 + |t|) (chi-square 0.08, 1 dof), and the even offsets read -0.022 and -0.012. The jobs charged 4.50 credits.
claims.boundary: One compile, one calibration set and two values of |t|; the |t| = 0.05 arm is underpowered, not a confirmation. The calibration-built simulator (depolarizing gates, readout errors, ALAP idle T1/T2) predicted odd parts +0.0296 and +0.0188 and even offsets near +0.029: the small-|t| odd part and the sign of the offsets depart from it, so its non-unital relaxation term does not describe this device. Heralding removes the active-reset excitation measured by iqm-garnet-reset-billing-pilot; it does not test the dark-probe law t^2/(2 + |t|)^2. The signed overlap equals t/(2 + |t|) for every unit vector u (signed-overlap-kernel-independence), so the run establishes that Garnet carries a relative pi phase on the signed branch through this compile, not a property of the sedenion kernel. Coherent gate errors add an odd term proportional to sqrt(|t|/(2 + |t|)) (iqm-garnet-signed-probe-coherent-response), so the single-visibility fit does not separate the linear law from that term: the measured ratio odd(0.05)/odd(0.25) = 0.26 +- 0.16 lies between the linear 0.22 and the amplitude scaling 0.47. The strong job lists its +t circuit before its -t circuit and the weak job its five +t circuits before its five -t circuits, so a reading that depends on batch position enters the odd part: a device with no signed response and a -0.044 shift on the second circuit reproduces the strong arm's +0.022, and the sign at |t| = 0.25 is resolved only under the assumption that position does not move the reading.

claims.statement: In the sedenions (cd_core) the signed dilation overlap <L_e2 u|(L_e1 + L_e10 + t L_e2) u>/(2 + |t|) equals t/(2 + |t|) for every real unit vector u, in the kernel of L(e1 + e10) or not, because L_e2 is orthogonal and L_e2^T L_e1 and L_e2^T L_e10 are antisymmetric (exact integer identities); as checks, the certified kernel vector (e4 - e15)/sqrt2, the bright vector (e4 + e15)/sqrt2, e4 and a seeded random vector all read it, and on the kernel support {e4, e15} all 1000 seeded replacement sign tables leave it unchanged. The zero-divisor property is instead the eigenvalue -1 of K = L_e1^T L_e10 on u (K swaps e4 and e15, and its -1 eigenspace is four-dimensional): the cancellation observable cos^2(theta) <w|L_e1 u> + sin^2(theta) <w|L_e10 u> with w = L_e1 u reads cos(2 theta) for the kernel vector and 1 for the bright vector, and one flipped L_e10 sign at e4 or e15, or 755 of the 1000 sign tables, removes its zero at theta = pi/4.
claims.boundary: Exact arithmetic over the listed vectors and the seeded sign tables; it says nothing about a device, and a hardware reading of the cancellation observable needs its own approved case.

claims.statement: For Cayley-Dickson dimension 2^n, n = 1 to 6 (cd_core), the sign f(p, q) in e_p e_q = (-1)^f(p, q) e_(p xor q) has algebraic normal form degree max(2, n) over the 2n index bits, with C(n, 2) + n monomials of degree 2 and (2^(k - 1) - 1) C(n, k) of degree k >= 3, and degree max(1, n - 1) in q maximized over the left factor p. Octonion left multiplication is therefore at most a degree-2 phase, implementable with CZ and Z gates, and sedenion left multiplication reaches a degree-3 phase.
claims.boundary: Enumerated for n <= 6; the closed form beyond n = 6 is a conjecture this certificate does not prove. Degree bounds the order of the multi-controlled phases a sign diagonal needs, not the routed CZ count on a lattice.

claims.statement: On the retained Garnet compile of the signed kernel probe (transpiler seed 2, 199 CZ on seven qubits), the first-order response of the measured <Z> on QB7 to coherent gate errors (prx over-rotation and axis error per qubit, residual Z after each CZ per qubit, CZ conditional phase per coupler) vanishes in the odd part at t = 0 for every error and grows with the signed amplitude sqrt(|t|/(2 + |t|)), not with t: the QB6 over-rotation coefficient per unit amplitude is -7.1, -6.9 and -6.2 at |t| = 0.01, 0.05 and 0.25. The even part responds at first order, led by QB11 over-rotation (-8.0 per unit relative over-rotation at |t| = 0.05), residual Z on QB11 (-1.56) and QB12 over-rotation (+1.15), Through the calibration noise model (exact density-matrix probabilities, each error inserted after scheduling) every response shrinks to 5 to 10 % of its noiseless size, unevenly (QB11 over-rotation -0.43, QB12 over-rotation +0.002): QB11 alone would need a 10.5 % over-rotation, three times the 3.5 % its randomized-benchmarking infidelity allows, and all 29 terms aligned at that bound move the even part by at most 0.032, short of the measured circuit-level -0.045.
claims.boundary: First-order derivatives of the compiled circuit, noiseless and through the calibration noise model, under a stationary error model (one relative over-rotation and one axis error per qubit, one residual Z per qubit after CZ, one conditional phase per coupler); angle-dependent, time-dependent and crosstalk errors and leakage lie outside it, and the noisy derivatives inherit the calibration model, whose even part the device contradicts. The device's coherent error magnitudes are unmeasured.
